text:
Lina Gomez: Heads-up: putting in for parental leave starting June 2. Quick question about benefits and the lactation stipend while I'm out — does Redwood keep paying the $200/mo stipend during unpaid company leave?

Ravi Patel: congrats Lina! :balloon: short version: the lactation stipend is considered a benefits add-on and usually continues if benefits enrollment remains active. You might need to request a benefits continuity waiver.

Lina Gomez: waiver? where do i get that?

People Ops (bot): Checklist: For benefit add-ons during leave submit the Benefits Continuation Waiver (BCW-2025) and attach the leave approval email. Deadline: 10 biz days before leave start. See: https://intra.redwood.com/benefits/continuation (internal link)

Maeve O'Connor: adding that payroll also needs the vendor ID for the milk supplies vendor. when i did mine i included invoices in the BCW and set the vendor tag to LACT-STIP.

Ravi Patel: exact workflow: 1) complete BCW-2025 2) email benefits@redwood.com with subject "BCW: Lina Gomez - Jun 2" 3) cc payroll@redwood.com with vendor details 4) request auto-pay flag if you want monthly direct payments.

Lina Gomez: i'm also on an H-1B and worried about benefits changes affecting my visa status. does unpaid leave or benefits suspension create any issues?

People Ops (bot): Immigration note: leaves of absence can affect visa maintenance in certain circumstances. Please schedule a 1:1 with People Ops + Immigration counsel. Use this calendar link: https://intra.redwood.com/sched/immigration-advice

Maeve O'Connor: fwiw i did the 1:1. they confirmed as long as your employment record remains active and you have approved leave docs, benefits changes alone didn't break status. but get counsel to be safe.

Lina Gomez: thanks. any special payroll codes i should ask for so the stipend isn't taxed weirdly?

Payroll Bot: Auto-reply: lactation stipend disbursements use payroll code LACT-STIP and are processed as non-salary benefits. Please include vendor EIN and monthly invoice.

Ravi Patel: also note FMLA paperwork if you're eligible — there's a separate FMLA packet (FMLA-Enrollment-Form.pdf) and sometimes state family leave applies too. that can change which weeks are paid by state.

Lina Gomez: i'm in CA so that might apply. do i need to file CA-PFL separately?

Maeve O'Connor: yes CA-PFL is separate and usually triggers from the state portal. benefits team can help coordinate the top-up so it lands with payroll properly.

Lina Gomez: last thing — coverage while i'm gone. i'm the hiring lead on the frontend role. should i reassign interviews or keep them in the schedule?

Ravi Patel: reassigning is best. create a short handoff doc in the hiring-runbook: status, candidates to progress, pending offers, and decision rubric. Maeve can cover interviews for 3 weeks; i'll pick up offers.

Maeve O'Connor: i'll take the early-stage screens. Lina pls leave notes about the rubric and any candidate red flags.

Lina Gomez: will do. also adding a Slack auto-response to my profile with return date and points of contact.

People Ops (bot): Reminder: submit BCW-2025 and FMLA packet by 1763104800 to ensure benefits continuity. Missing docs may delay stipend payment.

Lina Gomez: thanks y'all, submitting now. ping me if anything else is needed before June 2. :heart:
